content.rationale: The undo verb: a leading --help answers with the verb's own text (xlvoxmyl/rwlywqrk, per oqnsuzqu) and any other argument refuses, named (U1, puuvpqzl) — the surface is answered before the store is taken (H1, qtqnuqxo), so it answers on a root-less context, S3-root-required scoping the operation — otherwise it loads the marker state (M-markers-persist, wzyorrny), answers with the state undo leaves — the position one back — and the marker before the position (S5-undo-effect, zuqzrlrx), takes the inverse the kind names: a creation is removed by abandoning the change it targeted (D8a, prsoxsuo) through M-jj-abandon (urtkpxwv); a recording's journal entry is read through M-journal (zutqsqtu) and its before side applied to the target while the after side stays in the working copy (M-journal-apply, wmwkkqxl; D15c, mnwqksmt), the entry id recorded against the operation; a removal's entries are reverted newest first through the revert module (znmsuqlm, S3-revert kttmwrsv's mechanism), recording each revert's operation id, read through M-jj-oplog (mvwnksou), against the operation it undoes, and then writes the state it leaves (S5-save-after-revert, kqqysmxn), so a revert cannot take the record of the operation with it. A crossing that cannot spawn or fails refuses with its reason, naming the entry, and a revert that refuses partway reverts the reverts already made and refuses, naming the entry — qxmzpupt's semantics; each revert is then checked for divergence through M-jj-divergence (xoroywoy), and a revert that leaves a change with more than one commit is itself reverted, so the state returns to its pre-undo state, and the invocation refuses naming the entry (S5-revert-divergent, ppytsptl). The operation's selection is the marker before the position (D15, lummwqtx; G-select-undo, wwrrqtox; the linear history, kpptprql), whole-operation scope D8a's (prsoxsuo) over D8b's operation entries (txqmnvup), and never a partial revert is qmynqmwy's. A marker file that cannot be read refuses, naming the corruption (S5-refusal-site, tkqvkzsy), and a marker file that cannot be read or written refuses through the invocation that touched it (S2-markers-refusal-site, sprvousp); a position at zero and a position past the markers refuse inside M-markers-guards (lqtqzznn). The invocation never brackets (S5-lifecycle, vwlrqoxk) and writes nothing on success (O7-undo, tmxutlwm). It takes the injected context (M-context zttrwlts, M-context-injection ryuswoxz) and returns its lines — none on success — for the envelope to write (M-output-return, utrzvyyt) under M-route's handler shape (ynvwvzrm). I1-serde (orrvsxqq) fixes the JSON layer the module is written against — serde and serde_json, the crate's own `Value` and the derive. It takes the store through the context's fallible accessor for the operation, after the surface is answered (S3-root-required). And when that save cannot land the crossings already made are reversed and the invocation refuses, naming the cause (S5-save-failure, ntlspwxk) — so the graph and the marker file never disagree.
